onePager.heroTitle: How to build a website with AI
onePager.heroEyebrow: Copy · Content strategy · Websites built with AI
onePager.heroSubtitle: AI writes the code. Decisions stay on the human side.
onePager.heroLead: AI can write a website's code in a few hours. It won't decide what to tell your clients, in what order, or why they should trust you. That's my job: from decisions and copy to a working website.
onePager.heroPrompt: Build me a website for my law firm.
onePager.heroLastLine: // What should convince your client? No data.
onePager.aiRoleTitle: AI is a coding tool. Not a decision-maker.
onePager.aiRoleLead: Building a website has four stages. In the first three, AI can make suggestions, but it doesn't know your market, your clients or what sets you apart. That's why decisions, design and planning stay with people. AI gets the job where it's fastest: the code.

aiRoleCards.title: Decisions
aiRoleCards.text: Who the site is for, what it should sell, what we don't promise.

aiRoleCards.title: Design
aiRoleCards.text: Structure, order of sections, tone and copy.

aiRoleCards.title: Code
aiRoleCards.text: Components, animations, deployment. I review every change before it goes live.

onePager.problemTitle: The hardest part is the blank page
onePager.problemLead: You have a product or a service and you know more about it than anyone. Yet when it's time to write the homepage, you end up with copy that could belong to any company in your industry. AI won't fix that. It often makes it worse.
onePager.problemBefore: In today's fast-paced world, we offer comprehensive, innovative solutions tailored to your needs.
problemAfter: We handle inheritance cases. The first consultation takes an hour and ends with a written action plan.
Classes for groups of up to 8. In the first two sessions you'll learn the basic poses without risking injury.
We publish 6 books a year. Each one is edited twice before it goes to print.

problemGaps.title: Quality
problemGaps.text: The copy doesn't answer the questions clients actually ask.

problemGaps.title: Visibility
problemGaps.text: Search engines and AI assistants have nothing to quote.

onePager.problemClosing: Both gaps are fixed by the same change: copy that answers your clients' specific questions. People read those answers, and AI assistants quote them.
onePager.audienceRest: and need a website that explains what you do, without jargon and without exaggeration.
onePager.audienceText: I mostly work with businesses and people in niche, specialist and premium fields. They have knowledge their clients don't, and they need to explain it in a way that builds trust. In regulated fields such as law, health or supplements, I write within the limits: what you can promise and what you can't.

servicesItems.title: Website copy
servicesItems.text: A conversation that turns into copy for your homepage, offer, about page and FAQ. Or editing what you already have, including copy written with AI.
points: an interview instead of a brief you fill in alone
page structure and order of arguments
SEO metadata and FAQ for search engines and AI assistants

servicesItems.title: A website from decisions to launch
servicesItems.text: First we decide what the website should do. Then I build it with AI as a coding tool, on Next.js and Sanity, with a panel where you can edit the copy yourself.
points: a landing page for one service or campaign
a company website with a blog
a simple web app: forms, calculators, sign-ups
deployment on Vercel and a review of every change before it goes live

servicesItems.title: Content that keeps working
servicesItems.text: A blog plan and articles that answer your clients' questions and give AI assistants a reason to quote you.
points: a topic plan based on clients' questions
checking how your business shows up in ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini and Google

onePager.processLead: Decisions and copy take most of the time. The code comes quickly because I know what it needs to do.

processSteps.title: Conversation
processSteps.text: I ask about your clients, your offer, your competitors and what you don't want to promise. It takes 60–90 minutes.

processSteps.title: Decisions and structure
processSteps.text: We decide who the website is for, which pages it needs and what visitors should do.

processSteps.title: Copy
processSteps.text: I write the copy. You approve it before the build, not after.

processSteps.title: Building with AI
processSteps.text: I code with AI. I review every change, and you get an online preview.

processSteps.title: Launch and fixes
processSteps.text: Publishing, metadata, sitemap, first measurements. Feedback from the review goes in before launch.
